title: API Testing
sources: Python Automation Engineer Handbook (complete edition, Oct 2026)

challenges.title: Status for async work
challenges.description: A POST to SimpleUpdate starts a firmware update that will take several minutes.
challenges.instructions: Which status code best signals "accepted, still in progress" with a task to poll?
hints: The work has not finished yet.
Redfish returns a task monitor for long operations.
challenges.explanation:
202 Accepted means the request was accepted for processing but is not complete; Redfish services return a
       Location header pointing to a task monitor. 201 means a resource was created, 204 success with no body.
challenges.source: API & Protocol Automation Handbook Q6, Q18

challenges.title: Do not hard-code resource paths
challenges.description: A test uses /redfish/v1/Systems/1 directly and fails on a new platform.
challenges.instructions: What should the automation do instead?
hints: Resource IDs are implementation-specific.
Collections list their members.
challenges.explanation:
Redfish IDs vary by implementation (system, 1, sys0...). Start at the service root, follow the Systems link,
       and use each member's @odata.id, which keeps tests portable across vendors.
challenges.source: API & Protocol Automation Handbook Q13; Project 1
options: Discover members from the Systems collection's Members @odata.id links
Ask the vendor to rename its system

challenges.title: Walk a Redfish collection
challenges.instructions: Type exactly what this program prints. Each print() call is one line.
hints: rsplit("/", 1)[-1] keeps the text after the last slash.
The count matches the number of members.
challenges.explanation:
The comprehension takes the last path segment of each member link. Checking Members@odata.count against
            the actual list length is a cheap consistency assertion worth keeping in collection tests.
challenges.source: API & Protocol Automation Handbook · Redfish collections; Q4
challenges.code:
import json
body = '{"Members@odata.count": 2, "Members": [{"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems/sys0"}, {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems/sys1"}]}'
data = json.loads(body)
ids = [m["@odata.id"].rsplit("/", 1)[-1] for m in data["Members"]]
print(data["Members@odata.count"] == len(ids), ids[-1])

challenges.title: Read the health
challenges.description: Redfish resources report health in a nested Status object.
challenges.instructions: Write the expression that reads the Health value from the parsed response dict data.
hints: Status is an object inside the resource.
Index the outer key, then the inner one.
challenges.explanation:
Redfish puts State and Health inside a Status object, so the value is data["Status"]["Health"]. Using
           .get with a default avoids KeyError when validating optional properties.
challenges.source: API & Protocol Automation Handbook · Redfish resource model; Project 1

challenges.title: Safe concurrent PATCH
challenges.description: Two automation jobs might PATCH the same AccountService settings at once.
challenges.instructions: How does Redfish let a client avoid overwriting a newer change?
hints: The server labels each version of a resource.
Conditional requests compare that label.
challenges.explanation:
GET returns an ETag identifying the resource version. Sending it back in If-Match makes the PATCH
       conditional: if someone changed the resource since, the server answers 412 instead of overwriting.
options: Add a random sleep before every PATCH
Send the resource's ETag in an If-Match header; a mismatch returns 412 Precondition Failed

challenges.title: The test that hung all night
challenges.description: A nightly job hung for eight hours when a BMC stopped responding mid-request.
hints: What is requests' default timeout?
A server that accepts the connection but never answers...
challenges.explanation:
requests has no default timeout, so a silent BMC blocks forever. Always pass timeout=(connect, read), e.g.
        timeout=(5, 30), and let the framework convert the exception into a clear test failure.
challenges.source: API & Protocol Automation Handbook Q19; Python Automation Engineer Handbook · Ch. 27 API Testing with Python
options: resp.json() must be called before raise_for_status()
The request has no timeout, so requests can wait forever on an unresponsive server

challenges.title: 401 versus 403
challenges.description: A test user can log in but receives an error when trying to change NTP settings.
challenges.instructions: Which status code describes "authenticated, but not allowed"?
hints: One code means missing or invalid credentials.
The other means valid credentials without permission.
challenges.explanation:
401 means the request lacks valid authentication. 403 means the server knows who you are but your role
       lacks the privilege, such as an Operator trying a ConfigureManager action.
challenges.source: API & Protocol Automation Handbook Q14 (privileges and roles)

challenges.title: Redfish session lifecycle
challenges.description: Session authentication avoids sending the password with every request.
challenges.instructions: Order the steps of a well-behaved Redfish session.
hints: You cannot use a token before you have received it.
Clean up at the end.
challenges.explanation:
Creating a session returns a token and the session's URI. The token authenticates later requests;
            deleting the session at the end frees one of the BMC's limited session slots.
challenges.source: API & Protocol Automation Handbook Q17; Project 1
steps: Read X-Auth-Token and the Location header from the response
Send X-Auth-Token with each later request
DELETE the session URI from Location when finished

challenges.title: Self-signed BMC certificates
challenges.description: Lab BMCs use certificates signed by an internal CA, and requests raises SSLError.
hints: Keep TLS verification on.
Tell requests which CA to trust.
challenges.explanation:
verify accepts a path to a CA bundle, so traffic stays encrypted and authenticated. verify=False disables
       certificate checks and invites man-in-the-middle attacks, even in labs.
challenges.source: API & Protocol Automation Handbook · Ch. 2.3 TLS, certificates; Ch. 34 Security (Python handbook)
options: Set verify=False everywhere and silence the warnings
Switch the BMC to plain HTTP
Pass the internal CA bundle: verify="/etc/lab/ca.pem"

challenges.title: Following nextLink
challenges.description: Simulate paging through a large collection.
challenges.instructions: Type exactly what this program prints. Each print() call is one line.
hints: The loop stops when get() returns None.
Page 3 is empty but still visited.
challenges.explanation:
The loop follows Members@odata.nextLink until a page has none. It collects 1, 2 and 3; the last page is
            empty and ends the loop. Always follow nextLink instead of assuming one page holds everything.
challenges.code:
pages = {
    "/p1": {"Members": [1, 2], "Members@odata.nextLink": "/p2"},
    "/p2": {"Members": [3], "Members@odata.nextLink": "/p3"},
    "/p3": {"Members": []},
}
url, items = "/p1", []
while url:
    page = pages[url]
    items += page["Members"]
    url = page.get("Members@odata.nextLink")
print(len(items), items[-1])
